units.title: Nice to meet you!
units.goal: Apresentar-se, trocar informações pessoais e falar de família, origem e preferências.
units.grammar: Verb to be · possessive adjectives · have / go / live / like
units.rule: Use am / is / are para identificar pessoas, falar de origem, profissão e estado. Os possessive adjectives vêm antes de um substantivo (my name, her brother). Have, go, live e like são verbos principais: eles não usam o verbo to be para formar perguntas no presente. Adjetivos opostos ajudam a descrever pessoas e coisas: friendly/unfriendly, quiet/noisy, good/bad, hot/cold.
units.formula: I am · You/We/They are · He/She/It is
forms: I'm from Brazil. / She's a designer.
I'm not married. / They aren't from Spain.
Are you a student? / Where is he from?
my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun
examples: My name is Alex, and I'm from Brazil.
Meu nome é Alex e sou do Brasil.
Her parents live in Recife.
Os pais dela moram em Recife.
We like music and sports.
Nós gostamos de música e esportes.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
Você tem irmãos?
units.function: Starting a conversation: Hello. / Hi, I'm… / Nice to meet you. / Where are you from? / What do you do? / How do you spell that?
units.pron: Sons e contrações de to be: I'm / you're / he's / she's. Em fala natural, a forma curta é muito mais comum do que I am / you are em frases afirmativas neutras.
units.mistake: ✗ She are my sister. → ✓ She is my sister. · ✗ What's your name? My name Alex. → ✓ My name is Alex.

practice.prompt: Complete: My parents ___ from Salvador.
practice.why: Parents é plural, então usamos are.

practice.prompt: Complete: I ___ from Brazil. (to be)
practice.why: Com I, a forma é am.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct possessive: Ana loves ___ family.
practice.why: Ana é she; o possessive adjective é her.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: He are my brother.
practice.why: He combina com is; o restante da frase permanece igual.

practice.prompt: Choose the natural reply: 'Nice to meet you.'
practice.why: A resposta convencional é Nice to meet you, too.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order: from / are / where / you / ?
practice.why: Pergunta com to be: question word + are + subject + complement.

practice.prompt: Where does Leo live?
practice.passage: I'm Leo. My sister is Clara. We live in Porto Alegre. Our parents are from the south of Brazil.
practice.why: O texto diz diretamente: We live in Porto Alegre.

practice.prompt: Complete the question: ___ you have a big family?
practice.hint: Have é verbo principal nesta pergunta.
practice.why: Com I/you/we/they e um verbo principal, usamos do.

practice.prompt: Choose the opposite of 'friendly'.
practice.why: Unfriendly é o oposto de friendly.

speaking: Introduce yourself in 5–6 sentences. Include your name, age, city, nationality and one interest.
Ask your partner three questions about family and where they live.
units.writing: Write a short profile (60–80 words) introducing yourself and describing two people in your family. Use to be and possessive adjectives.
units.reading: Hi! I'm Maya, and I'm Canadian. I live in Toronto with my brother, Sam. He's a university student, and I'm a chef. Our parents live in Vancouver. We love spending time together, but we don't live in the same city as our parents.

units.title: Work and family life
units.goal: Descrever rotinas, profissões e horários; fazer perguntas e falar sobre a rotina de outras pessoas.
units.grammar: Present Simple (he / she / it) · questions & negatives
units.rule: No Present Simple, acrescentamos -s ou -es ao verbo com he, she e it. Para perguntas e negativas, usamos does / doesn't e o verbo principal volta à forma base. Com I / you / we / they, usamos do / don't. Muitos nomes de profissões terminam em -er ou -or (teach → teacher; act → actor). Combine verbos e substantivos: do homework, have lunch, make dinner, take a break. Para perguntar horas, use What time is it? / What time does work start?
units.formula: I work · She works · Does she work? · She doesn't work
forms: He starts at 8. / They work at home.
She doesn't drive. / We don't work on Sundays.
Does he cook? / What time do you start?
Yes, he does. / No, they don't.
examples: My brother works in a hospital.
Meu irmão trabalha em um hospital.
She doesn't get up early on Saturdays.
Ela não acorda cedo aos sábados.
What time does your class finish?
Que horas sua aula termina?
I usually have lunch at one.
Eu geralmente almoço à uma hora.
units.function: Asking about routines and time: What time do you get up? / Where does she work? / How does he go to work? / What do you do? / What time is it? / It’s half past eight.
units.pron: A terminação -s da 3ª pessoa pode soar /s/, /z/ ou /ɪz/: works /s/, lives /z/, watches /ɪz/. Observe o som final do verbo. Pratique também dizer horas inteiras, e meia e e quinze: seven o’clock, half past seven, quarter past seven.
units.mistake: ✗ Does she works here? → ✓ Does she work here? · ✗ He don't like coffee. → ✓ He doesn't like coffee.

practice.prompt: My father ___ at a bank.
practice.why: Com he/she/it, o verbo recebe -s: works.

practice.prompt: She ___ (study) English every evening.
practice.why: study → studies na terceira pessoa.

practice.prompt: ___ your sister drive to work?
practice.why: Your sister = she; a pergunta usa Does + verbo base.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: He doesn't likes tea.
practice.why: Depois de doesn't, use o verbo na forma base: like.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct frequency phrase: 'I ___ have breakfast before 7.' (80% of days)
practice.why: Usually indica uma frequência alta, mas não necessariamente 100%.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order: time / does / start / what / work / she / ?
accepted: what time does she start work
practice.why: What time + does + subject + base verb + complement.

practice.prompt: When does Nina get home?
practice.passage: Nina is a nurse. She works night shifts and gets home at 7 a.m. She sleeps during the morning and has lunch at 2 p.m.
practice.why: A informação aparece no início do texto.

practice.prompt: Complete the negative: They ___ (not / work) on Sundays.
practice.why: Com they, a negativa é don't + verbo base.

practice.prompt: My parents usually ___ dinner at 7 p.m. (have)
practice.why: Have dinner é uma combinação frequente de verbo + substantivo.

speaking: Describe your weekday routine from morning to night. Add three time expressions.
Interview a partner about their job, work schedule and commute.
units.writing: Write an email about a typical working or studying day (70–90 words). Include at least four verbs in the third person if you describe another person.
units.reading: Daniel works in a small hotel. He starts at 7:30 a.m. and checks guests in. He doesn't work every weekend; he has Sundays off. His wife, Paula, teaches at a school and finishes work at 4 p.m.
readingQ: Which day does he have off?

units.title: Time off!
units.goal: Falar sobre lazer, hábitos, frequência e atividades favoritas; conversar sobre fins de semana.
units.grammar: Present Simple (I / you / we / they) · How often?
units.rule: Use o Present Simple para hábitos e rotinas. Com I / you / we / they, o verbo não recebe -s. Pergunte frequência com How often…? e responda com always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever ou never. Esses advérbios geralmente vêm antes do verbo principal e depois do verbo to be.
units.formula: Subject + base verb · How often + do/does + subject + verb?
forms: I don't go out on Mondays.
I often read. / She is always busy.
examples: I usually meet friends on Saturdays.
Eu geralmente encontro amigos aos sábados.
How often do you go running?
Com que frequência você corre?
They never play video games at work.
Eles nunca jogam videogame no trabalho.
We relax at home on Sundays.
Nós relaxamos em casa aos domingos.
vocab: dia de semana / fim de semana
units.function: Talking about free time: What do you do at weekends? / Do you ever…? / How often…? / What’s your favourite season? / That sounds fun! / I’m not really into…
units.pron: Atenção ao ritmo das frases com frequência: I SOMETIMES go swimming. A palavra de frequência normalmente recebe destaque, mas não deve quebrar o grupo verbal.
units.mistake: ✗ I go always to the gym. → ✓ I always go to the gym. · ✗ How often you go out? → ✓ How often do you go out?

practice.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
practice.why: Com to be, o advérbio de frequência vem depois do verbo: am never.

practice.prompt: How often ___ you play football?
practice.hint: Pergunta no Present Simple com you.
practice.why: Use do antes do sujeito em perguntas com I/you/we/they.

practice.prompt: Which phrase means 'duas vezes por semana'?
practice.why: A expressão idiomática é twice a week.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: She goes often to the cinema.
accepted: she often goes to the cinema
practice.why: O advérbio geralmente vem antes do verbo principal.

practice.prompt: Choose the natural reply: 'Do you ever go hiking?'
practice.why: A pergunta trata de frequência; responda com uma frequência.

practice.prompt: I ___ (hardly ever) eat fast food. Put the frequency phrase in the correct place.
practice.hint: Digite apenas a expressão que completa a lacuna.
practice.why: Hardly ever significa quase nunca e vem antes do verbo principal.

practice.prompt: Read: 'On weekdays, Eva studies after work. On Saturdays, she goes cycling. She rarely watches TV.' What does Eva do on Saturdays?
practice.passage: On weekdays, Eva studies after work. On Saturdays, she goes cycling. She rarely watches TV.
practice.why: A rotina de sábado é go cycling.

practice.prompt: Build the question: often / do / how / exercise / you / ?
practice.why: How often + do + subject + base verb.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct time expression: We usually go cycling ___ Sundays.
practice.why: Use on com dias da semana.

speaking: Talk about your ideal weekend. Mention three activities and how often you do them.
Find three things you and your partner both enjoy and one thing you do differently.
units.writing: Write a 'My free-time habits' post (70–90 words). Use at least five frequency expressions and one negative sentence.
units.reading: Tom has a busy week, but he makes time for hobbies. He plays basketball twice a week, cooks on Friday evenings and visits his grandparents every Sunday. He doesn't often watch television because he prefers reading.
readingQ: How often does Tom play basketball?
What does he prefer to television?

units.title: House and home
units.goal: Descrever uma casa, localizar objetos e falar sobre quantidades e espaços.
units.grammar: There is / there are · some / any / a lot of · this / that / these / those
units.rule: Use there is com substantivos singulares e incontáveis; there are com plurais. Some aparece com frequência em afirmativas e ofertas; any é comum em negativas e perguntas. A lot of funciona com contáveis no plural e incontáveis. This/these indicam proximidade; that/those indicam distância. Use How many…? para contáveis e How much…? para incontáveis ou preços.
units.formula: There is + singular · There are + plural · Is there…? / Are there…?
forms: There is a balcony. / There are two bedrooms.
There isn't a garage. / There aren't any chairs.
Is there a lift? / Are there any windows?
this chair · that room · these keys · those houses
examples: There is a small garden behind the house.
Há um jardim pequeno atrás da casa.
Are there any shops near here?
Há lojas perto daqui?
There are a lot of books on the shelf.
Há muitos livros na estante.
Those apartments are very expensive.
Aqueles apartamentos são muito caros.
units.function: Describing a place: It's on the second floor. / There's a park nearby. / The kitchen is next to the dining room. / How many bedrooms are there?
units.pron: There is costuma ser reduzido para there's na fala. There are não costuma virar *there're* na escrita formal; pronuncie o grupo com fluidez.
units.mistake: ✗ There is two bathrooms. → ✓ There are two bathrooms. · ✗ There aren't some chairs. → ✓ There aren't any chairs.

practice.prompt: ___ a supermarket near my apartment.
practice.why: A supermarket é singular, então usamos there is.

practice.prompt: There ___ three windows in the living room.
practice.why: Use there are com substantivos plurais.

practice.prompt: Choose the best option: 'Are there ___ restaurants nearby?'
practice.why: Any é comum em perguntas sobre existência/quantidade.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: There aren't some pictures on the wall.
accepted: there aren't any pictures on the wall
there are no pictures on the wall
practice.why: Em negativas, any é a forma comum nesta estrutura.

practice.prompt: Which demonstrative refers to several things far away?
practice.why: Those é plural e indica distância.

practice.prompt: The lamp is ___ the sofa and the armchair. (in the space separating them)
practice.why: Between significa entre dois elementos.

practice.prompt: Read: 'The flat has one bedroom, a bright kitchen and a balcony. The bathroom is opposite the bedroom.' Where is the bathroom?
practice.passage: The flat has one bedroom, a bright kitchen and a balcony. The bathroom is opposite the bedroom.
practice.why: O texto usa a expressão opposite the bedroom.

practice.prompt: Build the question: any / are / there / cupboards / ?
practice.why: Are there + any + plural noun.

practice.prompt: There are ___ of books on the shelves. (muitas)
practice.hint: Expressão de quantidade usada com substantivos contáveis e incontáveis.
practice.why: A lot of pode ser usado com plurais contáveis e incontáveis.

speaking: Describe your bedroom or another room. Mention furniture and where three objects are.
Ask a partner about their ideal home: location, number of rooms and special features.
units.writing: Describe an imaginary apartment (80–100 words). Include there is/are, some/any and at least four prepositions of place.
units.reading: Our new apartment is small but comfortable. There are two bedrooms and one bathroom. The kitchen is opposite the living room, and there's a balcony next to the main bedroom. We don't have a garage, but there are two car parks across the street.

units.title: Super U!
units.goal: Falar sobre habilidades e possibilidades no presente e passado, pedir coisas com educação e conectar ideias.
units.grammar: can / can't · was / were / could · and / but / so / because
units.rule: Can + verbo base expressa habilidade ou possibilidade no presente. Could pode falar de habilidade geral no passado ou fazer um pedido mais educado. Was/were são o passado de to be. Use and para adicionar, but para contrastar, so para resultado e because para motivo.
forms: I can swim. / She can't drive.
He could read when he was five.
I was tired. / They were at home.
Could you open the window, please?
examples: My cousin can play three instruments.
Meu primo sabe tocar três instrumentos.
We were at the station yesterday.
Nós estávamos na estação ontem.
Could you speak more slowly, please?
Você poderia falar mais devagar, por favor?
I stayed home because it was raining.
Fiquei em casa porque estava chovendo.
She couldn’t swim when she was five.
Ela não sabia nadar quando tinha cinco anos.
I was tired, so I went to bed early.
Eu estava cansado, então fui dormir cedo.
units.function: Polite requests: Can you help me? / Could you repeat that, please? / Could I borrow your pen? / Sure. / Of course. / I'm afraid I can't.
units.pron: Can costuma ser reduzido em frases afirmativas (I can swim), enquanto can't recebe mais destaque. Pratique a diferença entre o som final de can e can't sem exagerar a vogal.
units.mistake: ✗ She can to dance. → ✓ She can dance. · ✗ Could you to help me? → ✓ Could you help me?

practice.prompt: My little brother ___ swim very well.
practice.why: Can é modal e vem seguido diretamente do verbo base.

practice.prompt: When I was six, I ___ (can) ride a bike.
practice.why: Could é a forma passada de can para habilidade geral.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct past form: We ___ at home last night.
practice.why: We combina com were no passado.

practice.prompt: Which request is more polite?
options: Could you open the door, please?
practice.why: Could you… please? é uma forma educada de pedir.

practice.prompt: I was hungry, ___ I made a sandwich. (result)
practice.why: So introduz o resultado: eu estava com fome, então fiz um sanduíche.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: They wasn't at school yesterday.
accepted: they were not at school yesterday
practice.why: They exige were; a negativa contraída é weren't.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct response to 'Could I use your phone?'
practice.why: Yes, of course é uma resposta natural a um pedido educado.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence: couldn't / yesterday / because / I / come / sick / was / I
accepted: I couldn't come yesterday because I was sick
practice.why: Could not + base verb; because introduz a razão.

practice.prompt: Choose the best connector: I can play the piano, ___ I can't play the guitar.
practice.why: But introduz contraste entre duas informações.

speaking: List five things you can do and two things you can't do. Ask your partner about their abilities.
Role-play: ask a classmate politely to lend you a pen, repeat a sentence and close the window.
units.writing: Write a short paragraph about what you could do as a child, what you can do now and one thing you would like to learn.
units.reading: When Omar was a child, he could climb trees and ride a bike, but he couldn't swim. Now he can swim very well. Last summer, he was at a sports camp, and he made new friends because he joined the swimming team.
readingQ: What couldn't Omar do as a child?
Why did he make new friends at camp?

units.title: Lessons in life
units.goal: Contar experiências passadas, falar de acontecimentos e expressar sentimentos.
units.grammar: Past Simple · regular & irregular verbs · -ed pronunciation · articles
units.rule: Use o Past Simple para ações concluídas em um período passado. Verbos regulares recebem -ed; irregulares têm formas próprias. Em perguntas e negativas, use did/didn't + forma base. Adjetivos em -ed descrevem como alguém se sente; -ing descreve o que provoca o sentimento. Use a/an com substantivo singular contável não específico (a hotel, an invitation); the quando o referente é específico ou conhecido (the hotel we booked); sem artigo em generalizações com plurais e incontáveis (Music is important; Dogs need exercise).
units.formula: Affirmative: subject + past verb · Did + subject + base verb? · didn't + base verb
forms: go → went · buy → bought · see → saw
examples: We visited our grandparents last weekend.
Visitamos nossos avós no fim de semana passado.
She bought a new phone yesterday.
Ela comprou um celular novo ontem.
Did you see the match?
Você assistiu à partida?
I was surprised by the news.
Fiquei surpreso com a notícia.
units.function: Talking about dates and past events: When was it? / It was on May 3rd. / What happened? / It was exciting. / I had a great time.
units.pron: A terminação -ed tem três sons: /t/ em worked, /d/ em played e /ɪd/ em wanted. A pronúncia depende do som final do verbo, não apenas da letra.
units.mistake: ✗ Did you went? → ✓ Did you go? · ✗ I was boring at the party. → ✓ I was bored at the party. (Boring descreve a festa.)

practice.prompt: Last night, we ___ a great film.
practice.why: See é irregular: see → saw → seen. No Past Simple usamos saw.

practice.prompt: They ___ (visit) their aunt two days ago.
practice.why: Visit + -ed = visited.

practice.prompt: ___ you enjoy the concert?
practice.why: Perguntas no Past Simple com verbo principal usam did + base verb.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: She didn't bought a ticket.
practice.why: Depois de didn't, o verbo fica na forma base: buy.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct adjective: 'The film was very ___; I couldn't stop watching.'
practice.why: Exciting descreve algo que causa entusiasmo; excited descreve a pessoa.

practice.prompt: Which verb has the /ɪd/ ending in the past?
practice.why: Wanted termina em /ɪd/ porque o verbo base termina no som /t/.

practice.prompt: Build the question: did / where / go / you / yesterday / ?
practice.why: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb.

practice.prompt: Read: 'Last April, Mia travelled to Chile. She visited Santiago and tried local food. She was nervous before the flight, but the trip was exciting.' How did Mia feel before the flight?
practice.passage: Last April, Mia travelled to Chile. She visited Santiago and tried local food. She was nervous before the flight, but the trip was exciting.
practice.why: O texto afirma que ela was nervous antes do voo.

practice.prompt: We stayed in ___ hotel near the airport. (article)
practice.hint: Substantivo singular contável, menção não específica; som inicial de hotel /h/.
practice.why: Use a antes de hotel quando ele é mencionado pela primeira vez e não é específico.

speaking: Tell a short story about a memorable day. Use at least five past verbs and two feeling adjectives.
Ask and answer: Where were you last weekend? What did you do? Who did you meet?
units.writing: Write a 90–110-word story about a memorable day. Include when it happened, what you did and how you felt.
units.reading: Two years ago, Ben moved to a new town. At first, he felt worried because he didn't know anyone. He joined a music group, met friendly people and learned to play the guitar. Now he says moving was one of the best decisions of his life.
readingQ: Why was Ben worried at first?
What did he learn to play?

units.title: Remember when…
units.goal: Fazer perguntas sobre o passado, descrever ocasiões especiais e organizar acontecimentos no tempo.
units.grammar: Past Simple questions & negatives · in / on / at / ago · adverbs
units.rule: Use did/didn't com verbos principais no passado. Use in com meses, anos e partes do dia; on com dias e datas; at com horários e alguns períodos fixos. Ago indica quanto tempo antes do presente e normalmente vem no final (two years ago). Muitos advérbios de modo são formados com adjective + -ly e descrevem como uma ação acontece.
units.formula: Did + subject + base verb? · didn't + base verb · in / on / at + time
forms: What did you do on your birthday?
in July · on Saturday · at night · two days ago
examples: I met my best friend at a festival in 2022.
Conheci meu melhor amigo em um festival em 2022.
The ceremony started at 6 p.m.
A cerimônia começou às 18h.
We travelled on Friday.
Nós viajamos na sexta-feira.
She spoke quietly during the film.
Ela falou baixinho durante o filme.
units.function: Talking about special occasions: When was it? / Who was there? / What did you wear? / Did you enjoy it? / It was unforgettable.
units.pron: Em palavras terminadas em -ly, mantenha o sufixo leve, sem acrescentar uma sílaba extra. Compare quick e quickly; careful e carefully.
units.mistake: ✗ I met him in Monday. → ✓ I met him on Monday. · ✗ Did she called? → ✓ Did she call?

practice.prompt: We got married ___ June.
practice.why: Use in com meses: in June.

practice.prompt: The party starts ___ 8:30.
practice.why: Use at com horários específicos.

practice.prompt: I saw that film three days ___.
practice.hint: Expressão para indicar distância no passado.
practice.why: Ago vem depois da quantidade de tempo.

practice.prompt: Correct the question: Did they arrived early?
practice.why: Depois de did, use o verbo base arrive.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct adverb: 'Please drive ___. The road is wet.'
practice.why: Para descrever como alguém dirige, precisamos de um advérbio: carefully.

practice.prompt: Which preposition is correct? 'The event is ___ Saturday.'
practice.why: Use on com dias da semana.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order: what / happened / at the wedding / ?
accepted: what did happen at the wedding
practice.why: A forma neutra é What happened…?; também é possível usar did para ênfase.

practice.prompt: Read: 'The graduation was on Friday evening. The guests arrived at 7 p.m. and the ceremony finished two hours later.' When did the guests arrive?
practice.passage: The graduation was on Friday evening. The guests arrived at 7 p.m. and the ceremony finished two hours later.
practice.why: O texto indica 7 p.m.

practice.prompt: They moved to London three years ___.
practice.hint: Palavra que indica quanto tempo antes do presente.
practice.why: Ago normalmente aparece no fim da expressão de tempo: three years ago.

speaking: Describe a special occasion you remember. Say when it happened, who was there and what happened.
Interview your partner about a celebration using at least four Past Simple questions.
units.writing: Write an invitation to a special event (60–80 words). Then write a short memory about an event you attended.
units.reading: Last October, we went to my cousin's wedding. The ceremony was in a beautiful garden, and the reception started at 7 p.m. Everyone dressed elegantly. The band played loudly, but the speeches were surprisingly emotional.

units.title: Love it or hate it!
units.goal: Falar sobre gostos, pedir comida, descrever quantidades e fazer compras.
units.grammar: would like · like + noun / -ing · countable & uncountable nouns · some / any / much / many
units.rule: Like expressa preferência geral: I like coffee / I like cooking. Would like é um desejo ou pedido mais específico: I'd like a coffee / I'd like to order. Use a/an com um substantivo singular contável (a sandwich, an apple) e some com plural ou incontável em afirmativas e ofertas (some apples, some water). Many combina com contáveis no plural; much com incontáveis. Any é comum em negativas e perguntas.
units.formula: would like + noun / to + verb · many + plural countable · much + uncountable
forms: I like vegetables. / I like cooking.
I'd like a table for two, please.
How many apples? / How much milk?
examples: I'd like to try the vegetable soup.
Eu gostaria de experimentar a sopa de legumes.
We don't have any rice left.
Não temos mais arroz.
How many eggs do we need?
De quantos ovos precisamos?
There isn't much sugar in this recipe.
Não há muito açúcar nesta receita.
units.function: Shopping and ordering: Can I have…? / I'd like… / How much is it? / Anything else? / That's all, thanks. / Could we have the bill, please?
units.pron: Would you like…? costuma soar conectado: /wʊdʒə laɪk/. Pratique a pergunta inteira, mantendo o ritmo natural em vez de pronunciar cada palavra isoladamente.
units.mistake: ✗ I'd like a have coffee. → ✓ I'd like to have a coffee. · ✗ How many milk? → ✓ How much milk?

practice.prompt: I'd ___ a glass of water, please.
practice.why: A estrutura é would like + substantivo.

practice.prompt: How ___ apples do we need?
practice.why: Apples é contável e está no plural; use many.

practice.prompt: There isn't ___ cheese in the fridge.
practice.why: Much é usado com substantivos incontáveis em perguntas e negativas.

practice.prompt: Choose the natural offer.
options: Do you like some coffee now?
practice.why: Some é natural em ofertas: Would you like some…?

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: I would like a buy a sandwich.
accepted: i would like to buy a sandwich
i'd like to buy a sandwich
practice.why: Depois de would like, use to + verbo para expressar uma ação desejada.

practice.prompt: Which noun is uncountable in this context?
practice.why: Bread é normalmente incontável; podemos dizer a loaf of bread.

practice.prompt: At a shop: 'How much are these oranges?' — choose the best reply.
practice.why: A pergunta pede preço; a resposta apresenta o valor.

practice.prompt: Build the request: like / I'd / to order / a salad / please
accepted: i'd like to order a salad please
i would like to order a salad please
practice.why: Would like + to + base verb + object.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct request at a restaurant.
options: I'd like a glass of water, please.
I like a glass water yesterday.
practice.why: I'd like + noun é uma forma educada de pedir algo.

speaking: Role-play a café order. Ask for a drink and a meal, then ask for the bill.
Talk about three foods you love, two you dislike and something you would like to try.
units.writing: Create a shopping list for a meal for four people. Then write a short message explaining what you would like to cook and what quantities you need.
units.reading: At Green Café, the lunch menu includes soup, sandwiches and salads. A bowl of soup costs $5, and a chicken sandwich costs $8. Customers can ask for extra vegetables, but there isn't much space inside, so many people take their food away.
readingQ: How much is the chicken sandwich?
Why do many people take their food away?

units.title: Life in the city
units.goal: Comparar lugares e pessoas, falar sobre características e dar orientações na cidade.
units.grammar: Comparatives & superlatives · have got · do / does / have / has
units.rule: Adjetivos curtos geralmente recebem -er / -est; adjetivos longos usam more / most. Use than em comparações. Have got expressa posse e muda para has got com he/she/it. Não confunda o auxiliar do/does das perguntas do Present Simple com have/has got.
units.formula: A is + comparative + than B · the + superlative · have/has got
forms: This street is quieter than that one.
It's the busiest area in town.
We've got a new library. / Has she got a car?
He hasn't got a bike. / They haven't got a map.
examples: The underground is faster than the bus.
O metrô é mais rápido que o ônibus.
This is the oldest building in the city.
Este é o prédio mais antigo da cidade.
Have you got a city map?
Você tem um mapa da cidade?
Walk along the river and go over the bridge.
Caminhe ao longo do rio e atravesse a ponte.
units.function: Giving directions: Go straight ahead. / Turn right at the traffic lights. / It's opposite the museum. / Cross the bridge. / You can't miss it.
units.pron: Em comparativos com -er, o sufixo recebe uma sílaba: cheap → cheaper. Em more expensive, a palavra more carrega o contraste. Treine frases inteiras, não listas isoladas.
units.mistake: ✗ more cheaper → ✓ cheaper · ✗ the most tallest → ✓ the tallest · ✗ Has you got…? → ✓ Have you got…?

practice.prompt: A train is usually ___ than a bus in a big city.
practice.why: Fast é curto; o comparativo é faster + than.

practice.prompt: This is the ___ (busy) street in the area.
practice.why: busy → busiest (y muda para i antes de -est).

practice.prompt: Which question is correct?
practice.why: Com you, a pergunta é Have you got…?

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: This restaurant is more cheap than that one.
accepted: this restaurant is cheaper than that one
practice.why: Cheap é adjetivo curto; use cheaper.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct direction: 'Go ___ the bridge to reach the park.'
practice.why: Go over the bridge = atravesse/passe por cima da ponte.

practice.prompt: My town is ___ (quiet) than the capital.
practice.why: Quiet forma o comparativo mais comum com -er: quieter.

practice.prompt: Read: 'The old town is smaller than the new district, but it is more attractive. The museum is the most popular attraction.' Which place is the most popular attraction?
practice.passage: The old town is smaller than the new district, but it is more attractive. The museum is the most popular attraction.
practice.why: A frase identifica o museu como a atração mais popular.

practice.prompt: Build the direction: at the bank / turn left / and / go straight ahead
accepted: turn left at the bank and go straight ahead
practice.why: A instrução começa pelo imperativo Turn left e depois adiciona a segunda ação.

practice.prompt: Turn left ___ the traffic lights.
practice.hint: Preposição usada para indicar um ponto específico de referência.
practice.why: Use at the traffic lights para indicar o ponto onde virar.

speaking: Compare your town with a large city. Use at least four comparative adjectives.
Give your partner directions from a station to a museum using four location phrases.
units.writing: Write a short city guide (90–110 words) comparing two neighbourhoods and recommending three places to visit.
units.reading: Riverside is a small town, but it has got a beautiful market and a long walking path. The capital is much bigger and noisier. However, Riverside is cheaper and the people are friendlier. The oldest building is the town hall, opposite the main square.

units.title: What are you up to?
units.goal: Descrever o que está acontecendo agora, contrastar hábitos e ações temporárias e falar sobre aparência e roupas.
units.grammar: Present Continuous · Present Simple vs Continuous · whose / who’s · possessive pronouns
units.rule: Use Present Continuous para ações acontecendo agora ou situações temporárias: am/is/are + verb-ing. Use Present Simple para hábitos e fatos. Whose pergunta sobre posse; who's significa who is. Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) substituem o substantivo. A forma -ing também pode funcionar como substantivo para nomear uma atividade: Swimming is fun; I love reading.
units.formula: am / is / are + verb-ing · Whose + noun? · This is mine.
forms: Whose jacket is this? It's mine.
examples: I'm talking to a friend at the moment.
Estou conversando com um amigo neste momento.
He usually wears jeans, but today he's wearing a suit.
Ele geralmente usa jeans, mas hoje está usando terno.
Whose keys are these?
De quem são estas chaves?
That blue bag is hers.
Aquela bolsa azul é dela.
units.function: Social English: What are you up to? / I'm just… / Are you busy? / Not at all. / Sorry, I can't talk right now. / No problem.
units.pron: O final -ing deve ser conectado ao verbo sem adicionar uma sílaba extra. Em frases rápidas, am/is/are podem ser reduzidos: I'm, she's, they're.
units.mistake: ✗ What you are doing? → ✓ What are you doing? · ✗ This is her's. → ✓ This is hers. · ✗ Who's phone is this? → ✓ Whose phone is this?

practice.prompt: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
practice.why: Look! indica ação acontecendo agora; use are + -ing.

practice.prompt: My dad usually ___ coffee, but today he's drinking tea.
practice.why: Usually indica hábito; use Present Simple com he: drinks.

practice.prompt: What ___ you doing right now?
practice.why: A pergunta usa are + subject + verb-ing.

practice.prompt: ___ shoes are these? They look new.
practice.why: Whose pergunta a quem pertence algo.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: This phone is her.
practice.why: Hers é o pronome possessivo que substitui her phone.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He's wearing a blue jacket today.
He wearing a blue jacket today.
He is wear a blue jacket today.
He wears a blue jacket right now.
practice.why: Ação temporária agora: is wearing.

practice.prompt: Read: 'Marta works in an office, but this week she's working from home. She's wearing comfortable clothes today.' Where is Marta working this week?
practice.passage: Marta works in an office, but this week she's working from home. She's wearing comfortable clothes today.
practice.why: A situação temporária desta semana é trabalhar de casa.

practice.prompt: Build the question: doing / what / you / are / tonight / ?
practice.why: What + are + subject + verb-ing; também pode perguntar sobre planos marcados.

practice.prompt: ___ is a good way to stay active. (swim)
practice.hint: Use -ing para transformar a atividade em sujeito da frase.
practice.why: Swimming funciona como substantivo/gerúndio: Swimming is a good way…

speaking: Describe what people in a picture or in the room are wearing and doing.
Ask and answer: What do you usually wear to work or class? What are you wearing today?
units.writing: Write a message describing what is happening at a place you are visiting now. Contrast it with what normally happens there.
units.reading: It's Saturday afternoon. Luis is meeting two friends in the city centre. One friend is wearing a red coat and the other is carrying a large backpack. They usually meet at a café, but today they're looking for a new bookshop.
readingQ: What are they looking for today?

units.title: Going for it!
units.goal: Falar sobre planos e intenções, compromissos futuros, previsões e motivos para realizar ações.
units.grammar: going to · Present Continuous for arrangements · predictions · infinitive of purpose
units.rule: Use be going to para intenções e planos decididos antes de falar e para previsões com evidência presente. O Present Continuous pode indicar compromissos futuros já combinados. Use to + verbo para explicar finalidade: I went to the shop to buy milk.
units.formula: am/is/are going to + base verb · am/is/are + verb-ing (arrangement) · to + verb (purpose)
forms: They aren't going to travel in July.
Are you going to apply for the job?
examples: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
Olhe aquelas nuvens! Vai chover.
I'm meeting my cousin tomorrow.
Vou encontrar meu primo amanhã.
She went to the pharmacy to buy medicine.
Ela foi à farmácia para comprar remédio.
Let's go for a walk. / Why don't we try that café?
Vamos caminhar. / Por que não experimentamos aquele café?
units.function: Making suggestions: Let's… / Why don't we…? / How about + -ing? / That sounds great. / I'm not sure. / Maybe another time.
units.pron: A contração going to é frequentemente pronunciada gonna na fala informal, mas escreva going to em atividades formais e textos. Em be going to, não esqueça o verbo to be.
units.mistake: ✗ I going to travel. → ✓ I'm going to travel. · ✗ I'm going study. → ✓ I'm going to study. · ✗ How about go? → ✓ How about going?

practice.prompt: We ___ visit our grandparents this weekend. We've already planned it.
practice.why: Plano/intenção prévia: be going to + base verb.

practice.prompt: Look at the sky! It ___ (rain).
practice.why: Use is going to com it + verbo base.

practice.prompt: We ___ dinner with Sam at 8. The table is booked.
practice.why: Present Continuous pode expressar um compromisso futuro combinado.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: I'm going study for the test.
accepted: i'm going to study for the test
i am going to study for the test
practice.why: A estrutura é be going to + verbo base.

practice.prompt: I went to the supermarket ___ buy some fruit.
practice.why: Use to + base verb para expressar finalidade.

practice.prompt: Choose the natural suggestion.
options: How about go to the beach?
How about going to the beach?
How about to go to the beach?
practice.why: How about é seguido por substantivo ou verbo em -ing.

practice.prompt: Read: 'The forecast says it will be sunny, so we're going to have a picnic. We are meeting at the park entrance at noon.' What time are they meeting?
practice.passage: The forecast says it will be sunny, so we're going to have a picnic. We are meeting at the park entrance at noon.
practice.why: The park entrance at noon é o horário combinado.

practice.prompt: Build the intention: going / I'm / to / learn / Spanish / next year
accepted: i'm going to learn spanish next year
i am going to learn spanish next year
practice.why: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb.

practice.prompt: Correct the arrangement: I meeting my tutor at 5 tomorrow.
accepted: i'm meeting my tutor at 5 tomorrow
i am meeting my tutor at 5 tomorrow
practice.why: Para um compromisso futuro combinado, use am/is/are + verb-ing.

speaking: Plan a weekend with a partner. Agree on a place, time, transport and two activities.
Look at today's weather and make three predictions using going to.
units.writing: Write a weekend plan (80–100 words). Include one intention, one fixed arrangement, one prediction and one purpose clause.
units.reading: On Saturday, Nina is meeting her sister at the train station at 10. They're going to visit a museum and have lunch downtown. The weather forecast says it's going to be windy, so Nina is taking a jacket. They want to go early to avoid the crowds.
readingQ: Where is Nina meeting her sister?
Why is Nina taking a jacket?

units.title: Have you ever…?
units.goal: Falar sobre experiências de vida, diferenciar passado definido e experiência sem data e conversar sobre viagens.
units.grammar: Present Perfect · Past Simple contrast · ever / never / yet / already / just · been / gone
units.rule: Use Present Perfect para experiências sem indicar quando, resultados ligados ao presente e períodos ainda não encerrados. Use Past Simple quando o momento passado estiver definido. Ever aparece em perguntas; never em afirmações negativas de sentido; already/just geralmente entre have/has e o particípio; yet costuma aparecer no fim de negativas e perguntas. Been sugere que a pessoa foi e voltou; gone indica que ainda está fora.
units.formula: have / has + past participle · did + base verb for finished past time
forms: Have you ever flown? / I've never flown.
She's just arrived. / I've already booked it.
Have you packed yet? / I haven't packed yet.
He's been to Rome. / He's gone to Rome.
examples: I've visited Argentina twice.
Já visitei a Argentina duas vezes.
I went there in 2023.
Fui lá em 2023.
Have you ever travelled alone?
Você já viajou sozinho?
She's gone to the airport; she'll be back later.
Ela foi ao aeroporto; voltará mais tarde.
units.function: Travel conversations: Have you ever been to…? / How was the trip? / What did you do there? / Did you enjoy it? / I haven't booked my ticket yet.
units.pron: Have you…? pode soar conectado, e as contrações I've / you've / he's são comuns. Dê destaque à palavra de experiência: Have you EVER…? / I've NEVER… .
units.mistake: ✗ I've been to London last year. → ✓ I went to London last year. · ✗ She has went home. → ✓ She has gone home.

practice.prompt: ___ you ever travelled by plane?
practice.why: Experiência sem data específica: Present Perfect, Have you ever…?

practice.prompt: I've never ___ (eat) sushi.
practice.why: eat → ate → eaten; depois de have usamos o particípio.

practice.prompt: I ___ to Mexico in 2022.
practice.why: In 2022 é um tempo passado definido; use Past Simple.

practice.prompt: She has ___ arrived; she's taking off her coat now.
practice.why: Just indica que algo aconteceu há pouco.

practice.prompt: Correct the sentence: Have you ever went to Canada?
accepted: have you ever been to canada
have you ever gone to canada
practice.why: Com Present Perfect, use o past participle. Para experiência de visita, been é muito natural.

practice.prompt: Tom isn't here. He's ___ to the station to meet his aunt.
practice.why: Gone indica que Tom foi e ainda está fora.

practice.prompt: I haven't bought the tickets ___. (até agora)
practice.hint: Palavra comum no fim de negativas/perguntas.
practice.why: Yet aparece no fim de negativas e perguntas sobre algo esperado.

practice.prompt: Read: 'Lara has travelled to Peru twice. Her first trip was in 2019, and she went again last summer. She has already booked a third trip.' How many times has Lara travelled to Peru?
practice.passage: Lara has travelled to Peru twice. Her first trip was in 2019, and she went again last summer. She has already booked a third trip.
practice.why: Ela já viajou duas vezes; a terceira viagem está reservada, mas ainda não aconteceu.

practice.prompt: We ___ (live) here since 2021.
practice.hint: Situação iniciada no passado e que continua no presente.
practice.why: Present Perfect + since + ponto inicial.

speaking: Ask a partner about travel experiences using Have you ever…? Ask follow-up questions in the Past Simple.
Describe a trip you have taken: where you went, when you went and what you did.
units.writing: Write a travel blog entry (100–120 words) about a place you have visited or would like to visit. Separate life experience from details of a specific trip.
units.reading: I've been to three countries, but my favourite trip was to Japan in 2024. I went with two friends and stayed for ten days. We visited Kyoto, took hundreds of photos and tried different kinds of food. I've already started planning another trip, but I haven't chosen the dates yet.
readingQ: When did the writer visit Japan?
Has the writer chosen dates for the next trip?

reviews.title: Checkpoint 1 · Units 1–4
reviews.subtitle: Identidade, rotina, lazer e casa
questions: Com you, use do para perguntas no Present Simple.
There ___ two bathrooms in the flat.

reviews.title: Checkpoint 2 · Units 5–8
reviews.subtitle: Habilidades, passado, lembranças e comida
questions: -ing descreve aquilo que causa o sentimento.
I'd like ___ a table for two.

reviews.title: Checkpoint 3 · Units 9–12
reviews.subtitle: Cidade, ações atuais, futuro e experiências
questions: This street is ___ than the main road.
Mine é pronome possessivo, substitui my bag.
At the moment pede Present Continuous.
We are going ___ visit my aunt.
Last Monday é tempo definido; use Past Simple.

before: What do you already know about London? Name three places, activities or forms of transport.
What questions would you ask a visitor about living in a large city?
during: Write down two places or attractions mentioned or shown.
Record one positive and one negative opinion about the city.
Listen for words connected with transport and movement.
after: Would you like to visit or live in London? Give two reasons.
Compare London with a city you know. Use one comparative adjective.

before: What does a bicycle messenger do?
What might make a working day in New York difficult?
during: Identify Alex’s job and the way he travels around the city.
Note three stages of his day: morning, afternoon and evening.
Write down one thing Alex enjoys and one thing that makes him tired.
after: Describe Alex’s routine using the Present Simple.
Compare his workday with a typical day in your life.

before: Name four jobs that involve helping people or creating something.
Which details are important when describing a job: duties, hours, workplace or skills?
during: Match each person to a job.
Note one responsibility for two different jobs.
Listen for expressions about working hours and free time.
after: Which job would suit you best? Explain why.
Describe a job using the Present Simple and at least three action verbs.

before: What makes accommodation comfortable when you travel?
Would you stay in an unusual building such as a tower or a bunker?
during: Identify the three unusual places to stay.
Note one distinctive feature of each place.
Listen for words describing location, facilities and atmosphere.
after: Choose one place and recommend it to a traveller.
Describe your ideal holiday accommodation.

before: What skills does a young musician need to develop?
Would you prefer to study music alone or in a school?
during: Identify the purpose of the music school.
Note two skills or activities the students practise.
Listen for expressions about hopes, plans and ambitions.
after: Explain what makes a good learning environment.
Describe a skill you would like to improve.

before: Which events from the 1960s to the 1990s do you know?
Ask a partner what important event happened in the year they were born.
during: Write down one event from two different decades.
Identify how people describe the events and their reactions.
Listen for past dates and Past Simple verbs.
after: Choose one event and explain why it was important.
Write three sentences about what happened in the year you were born.

before: What occasions do people celebrate in your culture?
Think of a special occasion you remember clearly.
during: Identify the occasions described by the speakers.
Note who was involved and what happened.
Listen for Past Simple verbs and time expressions.
after: Describe a special occasion using when, where, who and what happened.
Compare two ways of celebrating the same event.

before: Which foods are typical in your country or family?
What information do you expect to hear in a video about food?
during: Record three foods, ingredients or dishes mentioned.
Identify one restaurant or cooking-related detail.
Listen for countable and uncountable food words.
after: Describe a meal you enjoy and the ingredients it needs.
Role-play ordering food politely in a café.

before: What makes a city attractive to visitors?
Which features would you compare between two cities?
during: Identify the two cities in the video.
Note two places or activities a visitor can enjoy.
Record one similarity or difference.
after: Compare two cities using comparative and superlative adjectives.
Recommend one city for a weekend trip.

before: What time is it now in another country?
Why do people in different places experience different times of day?
during: Listen for the different places and local times.
Write down two activities happening in different locations.
Notice expressions with the Present Continuous.
after: Describe what people might be doing now in three countries.
Explain the difference between a time and a time zone.

before: What is a charity? How can people raise money for a cause?
Would you take part in a long journey to support a charity?
during: Identify the purpose of the expedition.
Note the vehicle and one challenge or stage of the journey.
Listen for plans, intentions and future arrangements.
after: Suggest a charity project and explain its purpose.
Describe a journey you are going to take.

before: What counts as a memorable life experience?
Have you ever tried a new activity or travelled somewhere unusual?
during: Note two experiences described by the speakers.
Listen for Have you ever…? / I’ve… and Past Simple details.
Write down one experience you would like to try.
after: Ask a partner three Have you ever…? questions.
Describe one experience and say when it happened.
